financial-statement-analysis--exp-c5-sc3.prompt: An analyst ranks four firms on ROE. Firm X has the highest ROE at 28%, driven by a DuPont breakdown of 3% net margin, 1.2 asset turnover and 7.8 equity multiplier. For judging durable profitability, what is the best critique?

options.label: The high equity multiplier is a strength, because extra debt raises shareholder returns and the interest cost is covered by the asset turnover
The thin margin is the main concern, since turnover and the equity multiplier are fixed features of the industry and say little about ROE quality
ROE is mostly leverage-driven, so it is fragile; judge it against margin and risk
ROE is reliable here because a figure above 20% usually signals strong management, whatever the mix of drivers behind it

rubric: DuPont shows ROE built on leverage with a thin margin, raising risk.
Distractors treat ROE level or leverage as inherently good.

fluid-mechanics--cmp-c4-sc4.prompt: A siphon at sea level has its crest 11 m above the upstream water surface, and the outlet is lower than the surface. It will not run, even when primed. Why?

options.label: Atmospheric pressure acts only on the outlet, so a higher crest removes the pressure pushing water over the top and down the outlet leg
Gravity acts against flow above 10 m, so the water velocity at the crest drops to zero by Bernoulli and the flow stops there
The outlet leg becomes shorter than the inlet leg, so the pressure difference driving flow reverses and water drains back upstream
Crest pressure would fall below vapour pressure near 10 m, so the water boils and the column breaks

rubric: Pressure at the crest is about atmospheric minus rho*g*h, so it drops below vapour pressure before 10.3 m and the column breaks.
The other options misuse Bernoulli, leg lengths or atmospheric action.

fluid-mechanics--exp-c5-sc5.prompt: Two designs for a water supply line are compared at the same flow: A has a sudden contraction to a smaller pipe; B uses a gradual taper. Criteria: lowest head loss and least risk of cavitation downstream. Which is best justified?

options.label: A, because a sudden contraction raises velocity sharply, which raises local pressure and suppresses cavitation downstream, while the abrupt change adds only minor loss
B, because a taper limits separation and vena contracta losses, whereas a sudden contraction creates low-pressure zones
B, because a taper holds the velocity at the throat lower than a sudden contraction would, and the lower velocity cuts friction loss while cavitation risk is unaffected
A, because separation zones recover pressure efficiently, which lowers total head loss relative to a taper and also keeps downstream pressure above vapour pressure

rubric: A sudden contraction causes a vena contracta with low local pressure and extra loss; a taper avoids separation.
Distractors reverse the velocity-pressure relationship or claim separation recovers pressure.

fluid-mechanics--exp-c6-sc4.prompt: Design a pipe network upgrade. Constraints: a parallel pipe is added to an existing line so the total flow rises, and both pipes have the same end pressures. Which statement about the design is correct?

options.label: Head loss is equal across both branches, so flow splits by resistance and the flows sum
The head loss adds across the two branches, so the total loss equals the sum of both and the total flow falls
The flow in each parallel branch is equal, so the added pipe always carries half of the total flow, whatever its size
The pressure drop in the added pipe is zero, because the existing line already sets the end pressures for the network

rubric: Parallel branches share the same head difference; flows sum and split by resistance.
Distractors confuse series and parallel rules or assume an equal split.

fluid-mechanics--exp-c6-sc5.prompt: A pump must lift water from a sump to a tank. To avoid cavitation, design the suction side. Constraints: available NPSH must exceed the required NPSH by a margin. Which modification raises the available NPSH?

options.label: Lower the pump toward the sump level and shorten the suction line
Narrow the suction pipe so the velocity head rises and the margin increases at the inlet
Raise the pump well above the sump to give a larger static suction lift and more head
Warm the water to lower viscosity, which cuts friction and so widens the vapour pressure margin

rubric: NPSH available rises with lower static lift and lower suction losses.
Distractors worsen lift, raise velocity losses, or ignore that warmer water raises vapour pressure.

fluid-mechanics--prf-c5-sc1.prompt: A water line needs a meter for total volumetric flow rate. Criteria: accuracy within 1-2% of the flow rate despite a varying velocity profile, and the lowest permanent pressure loss among devices that meet this accuracy, because pumping energy is costly; purchase price is secondary. Which device best meets the criteria?

options.label: Venturi meter
Pitot tube at the centreline
Sharp-edged orifice plate
Partly closed valve with a gauge

rubric: A venturi recovers most of the pressure downstream, so permanent loss is low while accuracy stays high.
An orifice plate is cheap but wastes energy; a centreline pitot gives a point value sensitive to the profile.

fluid-mechanics--prf-c5-sc4.prompt: For fixed flow in a turbulent pipeline, friction head loss scales roughly as D^-5 while pipe cost rises about linearly with D. Which design principle for choosing D is best justified when pumping energy and capital cost both count?

options.label: Choose the diameter where marginal pipe cost equals marginal pumping saving
Choose the largest available diameter, since friction falls steeply with D and so total cost keeps falling as size increases
Choose the smallest workable diameter, since capital cost is certain while the future energy savings are uncertain and may not occur
Choose the diameter that makes Re just exceed 2300, since laminar flow gives the least friction loss per unit length

rubric: Total cost has an interior minimum where the marginal capital cost equals the marginal energy saving.
Extremes ignore one cost term, and the laminar-flow rule misapplies the transition value.

french--cmp-c3-sn1.prompt: You are emailing a hiring manager you have never met to ask for a meeting next week. You want a polite, correctly formed request in a formal register. Which sentence should you write?

options.label: Pourriez-vous me recevoir la semaine prochaine ?
Je voudrais que vous me receviez la semaine prochaine, merci d'avance.
Recevez-moi la semaine prochaine, s'il vous plaît, merci d'avance.
Peux-tu me recevoir la semaine prochaine, s'il te plaît, merci ?

rubric: Vous plus the conditional of politeness is the standard formal way to make a request.
Distractors use informal tu, or blunt wording (a demand or imperative) unsuitable for a stranger.

options.label: `function f(x) { return x * Math.random(); }`
`function f(x) { count++; return x * 2; }`
`function f(x) { return x * 2; }`
`function f(x) { console.log(x); return x * 2; }`

rubric: It returns the same output for the same input and touches nothing outside itself.
Distractors hide a side effect (logging, a counter) or non-determinism (random).

functional-programming--cmp-c4-sn1.prompt: A team replaces a loop with `data.map(parse).filter(valid).map(format)` on a list of 5 million records and sees memory spikes. Each stage builds a full intermediate array. Which analysis best explains the spike and a fitting remedy?

options.label: map and filter mutate the source array in place, so copies pile up as it grows; switch to a for loop that avoids copies
Chaining creates a new closure per record that is never freed, so memory climbs; avoid composition and call each function directly
The functions are impure, so the runtime caches every result it computes; wrap each step in memoization to cut the cost
Eager stages allocate intermediate arrays; fuse steps or use lazy iterators

rubric: Eager chained operations allocate intermediate collections; laziness or fusion avoids it.
Distractors misattribute the cost to mutation, impurity or closures.

functional-programming--exp-c5-sc1.prompt: You will split a large list into chunks, reduce each chunk in parallel, then combine the partial results. Judged on getting the same answer as a sequential reduce, which combiner and identity pair is safe?

options.label: String concatenation, identity empty string
Subtraction on integers, with identity 0 for each chunk
Pairwise mean of two values, with identity 0 for each chunk
Integer division on integers, with identity 1 for each chunk

rubric: Parallel chunked reduce needs an associative combiner with a true identity; concatenation has both.
Subtraction, mean and division are not associative, so regrouping chunks changes the result.

functions-and-graphs--cmp-c4-sc5.prompt: Let `f(x) = 1/(x - 1)` and `g(x) = sqrt(x)`. What is the domain of `f(g(x))`?

options.label: x >= 0 only, since the root is the only restriction
x >= 0 and x ≠ 1
x ≠ 1 only, since the root accepts every real
x > 1, so the root exceeds the pole

rubric: The inner root needs x >= 0, and the outer denominator needs sqrt(x) ≠ 1, so x ≠ 1.
Distractors drop one condition or misplace the exclusion.

general-chemistry--prf-c5-sc4.prompt: You need a buffer at pH 4.8 with good capacity in both directions. Criterion: choose the conjugate pair whose pKa is closest to the target pH. Which pair is best?

options.label: Acetic acid / acetate, pKa 4.76
Ammonium / ammonia, NH4+ / NH3, pKa 9.25
Hydrofluoric acid / fluoride, HF / F-, pKa 3.17
Dihydrogen phosphate / hydrogen phosphate, pKa 7.20

rubric: Buffers work best when pH is within one unit of pKa, ideally near it; 4.76 is closest to 4.8.
Other pairs have pKa values 1.6 to 4.5 units from the target.

genetics--exp-c6-sc5.prompt: A case-control GWAS draws cases mostly from one ancestry and controls mostly from another. It reports hundreds of hits at ancestry-differentiated loci. Which revision removes the confounding without discarding samples?

options.label: Restrict the analysis to common variants with minor allele frequency above 5%, where allele frequency differences between ancestries are assumed to be small enough
Apply a stricter Bonferroni threshold across all tested variants so that only the strongest associations survive, which filters out weaker ancestry-driven signals
Double the sample size using the same sampling scheme, so that the spurious ancestry-driven associations average out as statistical power increases
Add top principal components of genome-wide genotypes, or a relatedness matrix, to adjust for ancestry

rubric: Adjusting for ancestry through principal components or mixed models addresses population stratification directly.
Distractors alter thresholds or sample size, which leave the ancestry-disease correlation in place.

genetics--nov-c1-sn1.prompt: A clinic report lists a newborn's karyotype as 46,XY. A nurse is asked to name the baby's sex chromosomes.

options.label: Two X chromosomes, one from each parent
Two Y chromosomes, one from each parent
One X chromosome only, with no second sex chromosome
One X and one Y chromosome

rubric: XY means one X and one Y, the typical male pattern.
XX is the typical female pattern; X only describes a different condition.

genetics--nov-c2-sn1.prompt: A family pedigree shows two unaffected parents who have a child with a genetic condition. A student must decide what this suggests about how the condition is inherited.

options.label: It is dominant, and both parents carry a hidden copy that skipped them
It is caused by a new mutation in the child's body cells after birth
It is Y-linked, because the child is affected and fathers pass on the Y
It is recessive, and both parents are likely carriers

rubric: Unaffected parents with an affected child indicates a recessive trait with carrier parents.
A dominant trait would show in at least one parent.

genetics--prf-c4-sc2.prompt: In a pedigree (assume full penetrance), two unaffected parents have an affected daughter. Which inference is best supported?

options.label: Autosomal dominant; one parent carried the allele, and it was not expressed in that parent but was in the daughter
X-linked recessive; the mother is a carrier and the father's X chromosome contributed the second copy, unaffected
Y-linked; the allele passed from the father to the daughter and was not expressed in him until she inherited it
Autosomal recessive; both parents are carriers, so X-linked recessive is excluded

rubric: An affected daughter needs two copies; X-linked recessive would require an affected father, and a fully penetrant dominant allele would show in a parent.
Distractors misapply X-linked, dominant or Y-linked logic.

geometry--cmp-c4-sn1.prompt: A shop compares two cylindrical cans. Can A has radius 3 cm and height 10 cm; can B has radius 6 cm and height 5 cm. A worker says they hold the same because radius × height is 30 for both. Which statement correctly analyses the comparison?

options.label: Can B holds twice as much because volume grows with r²
Can B holds four times as much because its radius is doubled, and the halved height has no effect
Can A holds more because it is taller, and the height outweighs the radius
Both hold equal amounts because radius × height is equal for both cans

rubric: Volumes are 90π and 180π, so B holds twice as much; volume depends on r^2·h.
The worker's claim treats volume as linear in radius; 'four times' ignores the halved height.

geometry--nov-c2-sc1.prompt: Why does a triangle with angles of 50 and 60 degrees have a third angle of 70 degrees?

options.label: A triangle's angles total 360, so the third angle is 360 - 110 = 250, then halved to 125
Interior angles of a triangle sum to 180, and 180 - 110 = 70
The third angle always equals the average of the other two, which would be 55
Every triangle has exactly one angle of 70 degrees, whatever the other two are

rubric: Use the 180 degree angle sum to find the missing angle.
Using 360 confuses triangles with quadrilaterals.

geometry--nov-c2-sn1.prompt: A builder is laying square tiles on a floor. She finds that a floor 4 m by 3 m needs 12 tiles that are each 1 m by 1 m. She wonders why counting tiles gives the area. Which explanation is correct?

options.label: Each tile covers 1 square meter, so the tile count equals the area
Each tile adds 1 meter along the edge, so the tile count equals the perimeter in meters
Tiles are counted along the edges first, so the count of 12 is really 4 + 3 multiplied by 2
Each tile lies along the diagonal, so the tile count gives the diagonal length in meters

rubric: Area is the number of unit squares that cover a surface.
Confusing tile count with length or perimeter is a common misconception.

git--nov-c2-sc2.prompt: How does `git pull` differ from `git fetch`?

options.label: `pull` uploads your local commits to the remote, while `fetch` downloads remote commits
`pull` downloads remote changes and merges them into your branch
`pull` downloads changes for every remote branch, while `fetch` downloads only the current one
`fetch` downloads remote changes and merges them into your branch, while `pull` only downloads

rubric: `pull` is a fetch followed by a merge into the current branch.
`fetch` alone only downloads and does not change your working branch.

git--nov-c2-sn1.prompt: Alice and Bob both cloned a repository. Alice pushed a new commit to `main`. Bob then made a local commit on `main` and ran `git push`, which was rejected. What best explains the rejection?

options.label: Bob committed but never staged the file, so there was nothing for `git push` to send
Two people cannot clone the same repository, so Bob's copy was no longer valid
The remote has a commit Bob's branch lacks
Bob's commit message was too short, so the remote refused to accept it

rubric: The push is rejected because Bob's branch has diverged from the remote; he must pull first.
Staging and message length do not affect push acceptance.

giving-feedback--exp-c6-sc2.prompt: Design a team practice that meets three constraints: upward feedback becomes normal, it takes little extra time, and it does not expose junior people. Which design fits?

options.label: An open-floor 'feedback Friday' where everyone gives one critique aloud to a colleague, which builds the habit very fast and keeps it visible
A suggestion box reviewed by HR once a year, which protects identity and takes almost no time from busy managers or their teams
Managers ask for feedback on one named behaviour in each 1:1, then tell the team what they changed
A quarterly anonymous survey of 30 questions, with the full results shared at an all-hands to show real transparency to everyone

rubric: Asking about one behaviour in existing 1:1s is cheap and models the habit; sharing changes shows it matters.
Other options are costly, expose juniors, or are too rare to make feedback normal.

giving-feedback--nov-c1-sn1.prompt: Priya is preparing to give a team member feedback about missed deadlines. Her manager reminds her to start from a recommended first step in preparation. Which step should Priya take first?

options.label: Decide on the consequences she will announce if it happens again
Gather specific examples of the missed deadlines
Ask other colleagues what they think of him as a team member
Write a summary of the personality weaknesses behind his lateness

rubric: Preparation begins with concrete, factual examples.
Distractors skip evidence or shift to personality and gossip.

giving-feedback--nov-c2-sc2.prompt: Why does describing the impact of a behaviour help in feedback?

options.label: It makes the feedback sound more formal and so more likely to be taken seriously
It shows why the behaviour matters, which motivates change
It replaces the need to describe the behaviour itself, so feedback stays brief
It proves the person was wrong and gets them to accept blame and apologise

rubric: Impact links behaviour to consequences, giving a reason to change.
Impact complements, not replaces, the behaviour description.

go--exp-c6-sc2.prompt: Design a fan-out that fetches 50 URLs concurrently. The first error must cancel the remaining fetches and be returned to the caller, and no goroutine may outlive the function. Which design satisfies all of this?

options.label: Run the fetches sequentially in a loop and break on the first error, which trivially satisfies the cancellation requirement
Use `errgroup.WithContext`, pass its context to each fetch, and return the result of `g.Wait()`
Start a goroutine per URL with a `sync.WaitGroup` and write errors into a shared `err` variable that all goroutines assign
Start a goroutine per URL and return the first value read from an unbuffered error channel, leaving the others to finish

rubric: errgroup cancels the shared context on first error, waits for all goroutines, and returns that error.
Distractors race on a shared variable, leak goroutines, or drop the concurrency requirement.

go--nov-c2-sc4.prompt: What does `defer file.Close()` do when placed after opening a file in a function?

options.label: Waits for a background goroutine to close the file later
Runs Close when the function returns
Runs Close only if the function returns an error value
Closes the file immediately, then reopens it on return

rubric: Deferred calls run when the surrounding function returns.
Distractors misread the timing or condition.

go--nov-c2-sn1.prompt: A teammate writes `x := 10` at the top level of a file, outside any function, and the compiler reports an error. They ask why the same line works inside `main`. What is the correct explanation?

options.label: Integer variables can only be declared inside `main`, so other scopes need a function call
Package-level names must be declared with `const`, because variables need a function
`:=` works only inside functions; use `var` at package level
The name x is reserved at package level, so any other name would compile with `:=`

rubric: `:=` is function-scope only; package level needs `var`.
Other options invent restrictions.

graph-theory--prf-c5-sc3.prompt: You need an MST of a weighted graph with 2,000 vertices and nearly every possible edge present, stored as an adjacency matrix. You want the best worst-case time with simple code. Which choice is best?

options.label: Kruskal with full sorting, since O(E log E) is competitive and the union-find step adds little cost
Prim with a binary heap, since O(E log V) grows more slowly than O(V^2) once the graph has many edges
Dijkstra from one vertex, since the shortest-path tree it builds is a minimum spanning tree when weights are positive
Prim with an array scan, since O(V^2) matches the dense input and needs no heap

rubric: On dense graphs E is near V^2, so array-based Prim at O(V^2) beats heap-based O(E log V) and Kruskal's sorting.
Distractors apply heap or sorting advantages that hold only for sparse graphs, or confuse shortest-path trees with MSTs.

graphic-design-fundamentals--adb-c2-sc1.prompt: What does visual hierarchy do in a design?

options.label: It guides the eye through content in order of importance
It arranges elements in strict symmetry so the left and right halves match exactly
It limits a design to one typeface so that all text looks consistent in every section
It gives every element the same prominence so that no content is favored over other content

rubric: Hierarchy uses size, weight and color to signal what to read first, second and third.
Distractors confuse hierarchy with equal emphasis, symmetry or a single typeface.

graphic-design-fundamentals--cmp-c4-sc4.prompt: A brochure pairs two similar serif typefaces, one for headings and one for body text. Reviewers say it looks like a mistake rather than a deliberate choice. What is the best diagnosis?

options.label: Two typefaces are too many for a brochure, so the layout should be limited to a single face
The faces are too alike to contrast, so the difference reads as an error
Serif faces clash when paired, because their matching strokes compete for attention at every size
The heading face is lighter than the body face, so the hierarchy is lost and headings fade

rubric: Pairings need clear contrast in structure, weight or style, or a single family.
Banning serif pairs or limiting to one face is a rigid rule, not the cause.

hindi--cmp-c4-sc1.prompt: A learner writes 'मैंने रोटी खाया'. What is the underlying error?

options.label: खाया should become खाता, because a past action with ने needs the habitual form of the verb
The verb should agree with the object रोटी, so it must be खाई
The verb should agree with the subject मैं, so खाया is right but रोटी should be treated as a masculine noun here
ने should be dropped, because the first person subject मैं does not take ने in the simple past tense

rubric: In ने-constructions the verb agrees with the unmarked object, here the feminine रोटी.
Distractors assume agreement with the subject or that ने is optional.

hiring-interviewing--cmp-c3-sc2.prompt: You need a past-behavior question for the competency 'manages disagreement with stakeholders'. Which question fits that format?

options.label: Suppose a stakeholder pushed back hard on your project scope. What would you do first, and how would you handle it?
Would you say you are good at handling disagreement with stakeholders, and what makes you effective at it?
Tell me about a time you disagreed with a stakeholder over scope. What did you do?
What personal strength do you rely on most when working with difficult stakeholders, and why does it help?

rubric: A behavioral question asks for a specific past instance and its outcome.
The 'how would you' option is situational (hypothetical), and the others invite self-description.

html-css--exp-c6-sc4.prompt: A `display:flex` row holds an icon and a long title. The title must stay on one line, end with an ellipsis, and never push the row wider than its container. Which rules on the title meet all three?

options.label: `min-width:0; overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis; white-space:nowrap;`
`overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis; white-space:nowrap;`, which truncate the text inside the flex item
`flex-shrink:0; overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis; white-space:nowrap;`, which fix the title width
`width:100%; text-overflow:ellipsis; white-space:nowrap;`, which let the title fill the row and clip itself

rubric: A flex item's automatic minimum width stops it shrinking below its content, so `min-width:0` is needed alongside the ellipsis trio.
Without `min-width:0` the item won't shrink, without `overflow` nothing is clipped, and `flex-shrink:0` forces overflow.

http--exp-c6-sc3.prompt: Design cookie settings for a session on `app.example.com` that must survive a top-level link click from an external site, resist CSRF as far as cookies allow, resist XSS theft, and never travel over plain HTTP. Which attribute set fits?

options.label: `Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax`
`SameSite=Lax; Domain=example.com`, since a wider Domain makes the cookie Secure
`HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict`, since Strict also allows cross-site link navigation to carry it
`Secure; SameSite=None`, with no HttpOnly so the SPA can read it

rubric: Lax sends the cookie on top-level GET navigations, with Secure and HttpOnly covering the other constraints.
Strict withholds the cookie on cross-site navigation; None weakens CSRF protection; Domain doesn't add Secure.

http--exp-c6-sc4.prompt: Design an API change that renames a JSON field in `/v1/orders` without breaking old clients, lets clients opt into the new shape, and allows caches to keep both shapes separate. Which design works?

options.label: Return the new field and drop the old one, then send `Warning` headers to old clients so they know to migrate to the new shape
Change the shape for everyone on `POST` only, since GET responses are never cached and so cannot be mixed up by a shared cache
Serve the new shape as `application/vnd.shop.v2+json` via `Accept`, with `Vary: Accept`
Return `301` from `/v1/orders` to `/v2/orders` for every client, so each client upgrades after following the redirect

rubric: Content negotiation with Vary lets clients opt in while caches keep shapes apart.
Dropping the field breaks old clients; a redirect to the same URL is meaningless.

http--prf-c4-sc4.prompt: After login, the server sends `Set-Cookie: sid=abc; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict`. A user clicks a link in an email to the site and appears logged out on that first page load, but is logged in after refreshing. What explains this?

options.label: The session expired between the click and the refresh because no Max-Age was set, so the browser dropped the cookie after the first request
HttpOnly prevents the cookie being sent on navigations that start from outside the browser, such as links opened from an email client
SameSite=Strict withholds the cookie on the cross-site navigation; the refresh is same-site
Secure cookies are only sent once the TLS session is resumed, so the first request after a click goes out without the cookie

rubric: Strict omits cookies on cross-site top-level navigations; the refresh originates from the site itself.
HttpOnly only hides the cookie from scripts, and Secure only requires HTTPS.

http--prf-c4-sn1.prompt: A team serves `/app.js` with `Cache-Control: max-age=31536000, immutable` at a fixed URL. They deploy a bug fix, but many users still run the old script a week later, while a hard refresh fixes it. Server logs show no requests from those users for `/app.js`. What is the most precise diagnosis?

options.label: The CDN ignored the immutable directive and served a different file to those users, so the origin should purge its edge caches after every deploy
Browsers treated the cached copy as fresh for a year and never revalidated, so the URL needs versioning
The server sent no ETag validator, so browsers fell back to caching the script indefinitely and the server must add an ETag header to fix it
A hard refresh sends the request as POST rather than GET, which bypasses the stale copy that normal reloads keep serving from cache

rubric: A long freshness lifetime means no request reaches the server; fingerprinted URLs fix this.
ETag absence does not cause indefinite caching, and hard refresh does not alter the method.

hypothesis-testing--nov-c1-sc5.prompt: Which test is designed to compare the means of two independent groups?

options.label: Shapiro test of a single median
Chi-square test of independence
Binomial test of one proportion
Two-sample t-test

rubric: The two-sample t-test compares two group means.
Chi-square is for counts of categories, not means.

infrastructure-as-code--cmp-c3-sc4.prompt: Which configuration makes Terraform create a VPC before its subnet without using `depends_on`?

options.label: The subnet block is written below the VPC block in the same file
The subnet sets `vpc_id = "vpc-main"` and the VPC is named `main`
The subnet and VPC share identical `tags` block values
The subnet sets `vpc_id = aws_vpc.main.id`

rubric: Referencing an attribute of another resource creates an implicit dependency.
File order, names and tags do not affect the dependency graph.

infrastructure-as-code--prf-c4-sc4.prompt: An autoscaling group has `desired_capacity = 3` in code. A scaling policy changes the live value during the day, and every morning `terraform plan` shows a diff back to 3. Which diagnosis is most accurate?

options.label: Code and autoscaler both own the same attribute, so each run sees drift
The provider is buggy and miscalculates capacity, so a version upgrade alone would remove the diff
The scaling policy was created outside the code, so Terraform must destroy it before planning
The state backend is losing writes at night, so Terraform forgets the real capacity before each plan

rubric: Attributes managed at runtime should be excluded, for example with `ignore_changes`.
Distractors blame state or provider rather than dual ownership.

infrastructure-as-code--prf-c5-sc3.prompt: A reviewer sees a module that wraps `aws_s3_bucket` and exposes every argument as a variable, one to one, with no defaults or policies. Judged on maintainability and reuse, what is the best critique?

options.label: It adds indirection but encodes no standard, so it should enforce conventions or be dropped
It is acceptable as written, but only if the module is kept in a separate repository from every caller that uses it
It should be split into one module per argument, so that each individual setting can be versioned and released independently
It is ideal, because exposing every argument means callers will rarely need to edit the module or request changes to it

rubric: A module earns its keep by encapsulating decisions such as encryption defaults and naming.
Pass-through wrappers add cost without abstraction; repo location is irrelevant.

instructional-design--adb-c2-sc1.prompt: Which learning objective is written so that it can be measured?

options.label: Appreciate why the five steps of the returns process matter to customers
Understand how each of the five steps of the returns process works
List the five steps of the returns process in order
Become familiar with the five steps of the returns process in order

rubric: It uses an observable verb, so a learner's success can be checked directly.
Understand, appreciate and become familiar describe internal states that cannot be observed.

instructional-design--prf-c4-sn1.prompt: A hospital's mandatory medication-safety course shows 98% completion, yet error rates are unchanged. Interviews reveal nurses click through quickly. The quiz allows unlimited retakes with the correct answer shown after each miss. Which design feature most directly explains why quiz scores do not predict practice?

options.label: Completion tracking counts page clicks rather than time on task, so the 98% figure is meaningless.
Learners can pass by trial and error, so scores do not reflect skill.
Because the course is mandatory, learners cannot develop intrinsic interest, so they disengage from the content.
The quiz has too few items to give a reliable score for each nurse, so individual results vary by chance.

rubric: Retakes with answers revealed allow guess-and-check passing, so scores no longer indicate mastery.
Mandatory status, item count and tracking do not explain why passing fails to predict practice.

investing-fundamentals--cmp-c4-sc3.prompt: Over 15 years a fund beat the market by 1% per year before fees, yet the investor's account lagged a plain index fund. The fund charges 1.4% in expenses and 0.3% in trading costs versus 0.05% for the index fund. What best explains the lag?

options.label: The fund's extra return was taxed more heavily than the index fund's gain, which wiped out the 1% edge
Funds that beat the market in one period tend to underperform in the next, which cancelled the 1% edge
Extra costs of about 1.65% a year exceeded the 1% edge, leaving a net shortfall
The index fund held riskier assets, and the higher risk earned it a larger return over the 15 years

rubric: Net edge is about 1% minus 1.6% extra cost, around -0.6% a year, compounding over time.
Risk does not always pay off, taxes are not mentioned, and no rule makes outperformance reverse.

italian--adb-c2-sc2.prompt: In which situation would an Italian speaker normally use the formal pronoun Lei?

options.label: Chatting with a new classmate of your own age at university
Asking an older stranger for directions
Greeting your younger cousin when you arrive at a party
Texting your best friend about plans for the weekend

rubric: Lei is used with strangers, elders and formal contacts.
Distractors are informal settings where tu is normal.

java--adb-c2-sc3.prompt: Which of these is a checked exception that the compiler forces you to catch or declare?

options.label: `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`
`NullPointerException`
`IllegalArgumentException`
`IOException`

rubric: `IOException` extends `Exception` but not `RuntimeException`, so it is checked.
The others are runtime (unchecked) exceptions.

korean--exp-c5-sc2.prompt: A learner says: "해요체 is always safe, so I will use it in every situation, including a formal speech to a large audience." Which evaluation is most accurate?

options.label: Partly true: it is a safe everyday default, but formal speeches call for -ㅂ니다/습니다.
False: 해요체 is reserved for speaking to children and close friends, so adults always need -ㅂ니다/습니다 when addressing anyone older.
True: it ignores relative status entirely, so it stays acceptable even in formal broadcasts, news reports and official ceremonies.
True: 해요체 is the most formal register, so it cannot be too casual in any setting, whether a speech or a ceremony.

rubric: 해요체 is the polite-informal default; 합쇼체 is expected in formal speeches and announcements.
Distractors misplace 해요체 as the most formal level or as a children's register.

linear-algebra--prf-c4-sc2.prompt: A system Ax = b has 3 equations and 4 unknowns. Row reduction shows rank(A) = 2 but rank of the augmented matrix [A | b] = 3. What does this tell you?

options.label: There are infinitely many solutions, with two free variables because 4 unknowns minus rank 2 leaves 2
There is no solution because b lies outside the column space of A
There is a unique solution because the extra rank in the augmented matrix pins down every unknown
There are infinitely many solutions, with one free variable because 3 equations minus rank 2 leaves 1

rubric: Augmented rank exceeding rank(A) means b is not in col(A), so the system is inconsistent.
Distractors count free variables from the unknowns minus rank and ignore consistency.

linear-algebra--prf-c4-sc4.prompt: A student claims the eigenvalues of AB are always the products of an eigenvalue of A with an eigenvalue of B, and checks it only with diagonal matrices. Which statement best identifies the flaw?

options.label: The claim fails whenever A or B has a repeated eigenvalue, because the pairing becomes ambiguous
Diagonal examples hide that eigenvectors of A and B need not be shared
Products of eigenvalues only work when A and B are both symmetric, which diagonal matrices are not tested against
Eigenvalues of AB are always sums of those of A and B, which diagonal tests cannot reveal

rubric: The pairing of eigenvalues works only when A and B share eigenvectors (e.g. simultaneously diagonalizable); diagonal tests all share them.
Distractors name wrong conditions such as symmetry or repeated eigenvalues.

linear-algebra--prf-c5-sn1.prompt: A team ranks pages using power iteration on a huge sparse transition matrix with dominant eigenvalue 1 and second eigenvalue 0.99. Convergence is very slow. Constraints: keep the same matrix, keep it sparse, and avoid dense storage. Which remedy is best?

options.label: Invert the matrix once, then multiply the start vector by the inverse to jump to the dominant eigenvector directly
Restart power iteration from several random vectors and average the results to shrink the error ratio below 0.99
Use a sparse Krylov solver such as Arnoldi, needing only matrix-vector products
Compute the full eigendecomposition with QR iterations, since it is exact and the eigenvalue gap no longer matters

rubric: Power iteration converges at rate 0.99^k; Arnoldi/Krylov methods extract the dominant eigenvector faster with only sparse products.
Dense decomposition and inversion violate the sparsity constraint; random restarts do not change the convergence rate.

linux-command-line--nov-c2-sc1.prompt: You run `echo hi > f.txt` twice in a row. What does f.txt contain afterwards?

options.label: Nothing, because it was emptied
The word hi on two lines
The word hi once
An error, since the file already exists

rubric: `>` overwrites the file each time, so only one `hi` remains.
Two lines would come from `>>`, which appends.

linux-command-line--nov-c2-sc2.prompt: `ls -l` shows `-rwxr-xr--` for a file. What can users who are neither the owner nor in the group do?

options.label: Execute it but not read it
Read, write and execute it
Read and execute it only
Read it only

rubric: The last three characters `r--` are the permissions for others: read only.
Learners who read the wrong triplet choose the group's `r-x` or the owner's `rwx`.

llm-application-development--cmp-c4-sc5.prompt: Answers to policy questions omit conditions that appear two sentences after the retrieved text. Chunks are 80 tokens with no overlap. What is the likely cause?

options.label: Small chunks split conditions from the rule they qualify
Top_k is set too high, so the extra retrieved chunks crowd the conditions out of the prompt
The embedding model is too large to represent short passages well, so nearby chunks rank poorly
The vector index uses cosine rather than dot-product similarity, which reorders close neighbours

rubric: Tiny non-overlapping chunks separate a rule from its conditions, so only half is retrieved.
Larger chunks or overlap keep related sentences together.

llm-application-development--nov-c1-sn1.prompt: A developer's Python code calls an LLM and then runs json.loads on the reply, but the model sometimes adds chatty text around the JSON. The developer wants the API to constrain replies to a given schema. Which API feature is designed for this?

options.label: Lowering temperature to zero so replies stay deterministic
Increasing the max_tokens limit so replies are not cut off
Structured outputs with a JSON schema
Adding more few-shot chat history showing bare JSON replies

rubric: Structured outputs (schema-constrained responses) make replies parseable.
Other settings change randomness or length, not format guarantees.

machine-learning--exp-c5-sc4.prompt: Model A has AUC 0.91 but overconfident probabilities; model B has AUC 0.89 and is well calibrated. A downstream system applies expected-cost thresholds directly to predicted probabilities. Which choice best fits that criterion?

options.label: Recalibrate A on a separate held-out set, keeping its ranking
Use B unchanged, because a calibrated model needs no further checks and its probabilities will stay reliable after deployment
Use A as is, because its higher AUC means its probabilities will give lower expected cost at any threshold
Use B, because a 0.02 AUC gap is within noise, so ranking quality should not influence the choice

rubric: Cost thresholds need calibrated probabilities, and monotone recalibration preserves A's better ranking.
Raw AUC ignores calibration; calibration can drift, so B's status isn't permanent.

machine-learning--nov-c1-sn1.prompt: A team has a spreadsheet of past loans. Each row lists income, loan amount and age, plus a column saying whether the borrower defaulted (yes or no). They want to predict default for new applicants. What is the target variable in this dataset?

options.label: Income, because it is the main driver of repayment
The default column
Loan amount, because it sets the size of the risk
Row number, because it identifies each applicant

rubric: The target is the outcome to predict: default.
Income, loan amount and age are features used as inputs.

machine-learning--nov-c2-sc1.prompt: A model scores 99% on its training data but 70% on new data. What best describes this?

options.label: Overfitting: it memorised training noise
Data leakage: test set information reached the model during training
Over-regularisation: the penalty is so strong that it blocks learning
Underfitting: it is too simple to learn the training data

rubric: A large train-test gap signals overfitting.
Underfitting would give low training scores too.

mandarin-chinese--adb-c2-sc3.prompt: In the dialogue 我很好,你呢?, what does 你呢 mean?

options.label: Where are you?
And you?
Are you a person?
What are you doing?

rubric: 呢 after a noun or pronoun returns the same question: 'And you?'
Distractors confuse 呢 with 在哪儿, 吗 or a verb question.

mandarin-chinese--nov-c2-sc3.prompt: What does 我不吃早饭 (wǒ bù chī zǎofàn) most naturally mean?

options.label: I haven't eaten breakfast yet today, but I will later
I was unable to eat breakfast just now because I was busy
I don't eat breakfast, as a habit
I didn't eat breakfast yesterday, though I usually do

rubric: 不 negates habits, preferences and willingness.
Past or not-yet-done events use 没(有), which is what the other options describe.

mandarin-chinese--prf-c4-sc5.prompt: A learner says 老师说得太快,我听不见 meaning "The teacher speaks too fast and I can't understand." What is the error?

options.label: 见 is a resultative complement that marks any completed perception, so 听不见 already covers failing to take in meaning as well as sound
听不见 means cannot hear; failing to understand needs 懂, as in 听不懂
听不见 means cannot grasp the grammar, while 听不懂 means the sound is too faint or unclear to hear
听不见 is correct, but the potential form should be 听不了 to show that speed prevents the result

rubric: 见 marks perceiving sound; 懂 marks understanding.
Distractors reverse the meanings or claim 见 covers comprehension.

mandarin-chinese--prf-c5-sc2.prompt: A learner has 20 minutes a day and wants tones that stay accurate in connected speech, with some feedback. Which routine best meets these criteria?

options.label: Memorise a tone chart and the third-tone sandhi rules, then practise speaking aloud without recording yourself
Read pinyin silently each day so the tone marks become familiar by sight and by sound in your head
Shadow short native recordings, then compare your pitch with the original
Drill the four tones on isolated syllables until each is perfect before moving on to any sentences

rubric: Shadowing with comparison trains tones in context and gives feedback.
Isolated drills, silent reading and rule memorising do not train connected-speech pitch.

materials-science--exp-c6-sc2.prompt: A plan to strengthen a cast Al-4Cu part says: heat to 190 C, hold 8 h, air cool, put in service. Which essential step does the plan omit for precipitation hardening?

options.label: Preheating to the eutectic temperature to partly melt grain boundaries, which homogenises the copper before the ageing hold
Solution treatment above the solvus, then a rapid quench to a supersaturated solid solution
Cold work after ageing to dissolve the precipitates and raise dislocation density, so strain hardening replaces precipitate strengthening
Slow furnace cooling from the melt to grow large equilibrium CuAl2 particles, which block dislocations and raise hardness

rubric: Without solution treatment and quench there is no supersaturation, so ageing gives coarse equilibrium phases.
Other options describe steps that soften or damage the alloy.

mathematical-optimization--exp-c6-sc1.prompt: A production quantity x must be either 0 or between 10 and 50, and the model must stay a mixed-integer linear program. Which constraint set is correct?

options.label: `10 <= x <= 50` and `0 <= x <= 0`, joined by OR
`10y <= x <= 50y` with y binary
`x <= 50y` and `x >= 10(1-y)` with y binary

rubric: With y=0, x is forced to 0; with y=1, x lies in [10,50], and all constraints are linear.
The second option forces x>=10 when y=0; the third is nonlinear; the fourth is not a linear constraint set.

microbiology--exp-c6-sc4.prompt: Design an experiment showing that gene transfer between two bacterial strains occurs by transduction rather than conjugation or transformation. Which setup does this?

options.label: U-tube with a 0.45 µm filter and no DNase; transfer across the filter shows the agent is a phage, since cells cannot pass
Direct mixing on a membrane with DNase added; transfer still occurring shows the agent is a phage, since free DNA is destroyed
U-tube with a 0.45 µm filter and DNase; transfer still occurring shows a DNase-resistant agent
U-tube with a 0.02 µm filter and no DNase; transfer still occurring shows the agent is a phage, since cells cannot pass

rubric: The filter blocks cell contact while passing phage, and DNase removes free DNA, so surviving transfer implicates phage.
Distractors use a pore size that blocks phage, allow conjugation, or leave transformation unexcluded.

microeconomics--nov-c2-sc2.prompt: Which event would shift the demand curve for coffee to the right?

options.label: A rise in consumers' incomes
A new technology that lowers coffee production costs
A rise in the price of coffee itself
A fall in the price of coffee beans used by growers

rubric: Higher income raises demand for normal goods, shifting demand right.
Input costs and technology shift supply; own price causes movement along the curve.

microservices--adb-c3-sc5.prompt: A new feature awards loyalty points per purchase. Following service-boundary rules, where should the points balances be stored?

options.label: In a new Loyalty service that owns its own data store
In the Payment service's database, since points are calculated from the money spent
In the Orders service's database, since every point originates from a placed order
In the API gateway, since every purchase request already passes through it

rubric: Loyalty is its own business capability, so it should own its data behind an API.
Other options attach it to a service because of where the data originates, creating coupling.

microservices--prf-c4-sc2.prompt: A service saves an order to its database and then publishes an `OrderCreated` event to a broker. Occasionally the order exists but downstream services never hear about it. What is the root cause?

options.label: The event payload is occasionally too large, so the broker silently rejects the message after the order transaction has already committed
The broker uses topics instead of queues, so some consumers are never subscribed to receive the event when it is published
The order service uses an ORM, which delays commits until after the publish call has returned and so reorders the two steps
The commit and the publish are two separate writes, so a crash between them loses the event

rubric: This is the dual-write problem: no atomicity across the database and the broker; a transactional outbox fixes it.
Other options name plausible but unrelated configuration issues.

mindfulness-meditation--cmp-c4-sc5.prompt: Priya becomes more tense during breath meditation and notices she is trying to make each breath slow and perfect. What is the likely cause?

options.label: Her natural breathing rate is too fast, so she needs to train it slower first
She is sitting for too short a time, so the calming effect has not yet begun
She is controlling the breath instead of simply observing it
She has picked an anchor that suits her poorly, so she should switch to sound

rubric: Manipulating the breath adds effort and monitoring tension, whereas the instruction is to observe it as it is.
Distractors blame breathing speed, duration or anchor choice.

mindfulness-meditation--nov-c2-sc4.prompt: What is a realistic expectation after several weeks of 10 minutes of daily mindfulness practice?

options.label: Attention can stay on one demanding task for several hours without drifting
Stressful events still occur but no longer cause any bodily or emotional reaction
Thoughts stop appearing during sitting once the breath is followed steadily
Distraction is noticed sooner, though thoughts still arise

rubric: Practice improves noticing of distraction; it does not remove thoughts or reactions.
Distractors promise unrealistic total outcomes.

mobile-app-development--exp-c6-sn1.prompt: A team proposes third-party sign-in by loading the provider's login page in an in-app WebView and reading the redirect URL for the auth code. A client secret is embedded in the app. Reviewers say the design is missing a key element for security. Which change addresses it?

options.label: Obfuscate the client secret with string encryption and have the WebView check that the redirect host matches the registered callback before accepting the code
Use a system browser session (ASWebAuthenticationSession / Custom Tabs) with the code flow and PKCE, not a secret
Keep the WebView but move the client secret into the keychain or keystore, so the app can still read it to exchange the code and the user stays in-app
Switch to the implicit flow so no secret is needed and tokens arrive directly in the redirect URL, avoiding a code exchange step on the device

rubric: System browser sessions keep credentials out of the app, and PKCE replaces an extractable secret for public clients.
Obfuscation is reversible, implicit flow is discouraged, and auto-filling credentials worsens exposure.

molecular-biology--exp-c5-sc4.prompt: For quantifying a low-abundance transcript across samples, you need accuracy over a wide dynamic range and must control for sample input differences. Which design best meets these criteria?

options.label: End-point PCR run for 40 cycles, with gel band intensities compared against a loading control band
RT-qPCR with validated reference genes and efficiency-corrected analysis
RT-qPCR normalised only to total RNA mass, assuming equal reverse transcription and amplification efficiency in all samples
Northern blot with one exposure time for all samples, normalised to a loading-control band such as 18S rRNA

rubric: Efficiency-corrected qPCR with validated references gives wide, normalised quantification.
End-point PCR saturates; skipping efficiency checks and Northerns limit range or sensitivity.

molecular-biology--exp-c6-sc4.prompt: Design an experiment to show a distal enhancer is necessary for a gene's expression in its native context, rather than only sufficient in a reporter assay. Which plan fits?

options.label: Delete or silence the enhancer at its endogenous locus and measure target gene expression
Run ChIP-seq for H3K27ac and p300 in the native cell type and call the enhancer necessary from a strong peak at the site
Overexpress the gene from a plasmid lacking the enhancer and test whether the enhancer is still bound by its activators
Clone the enhancer upstream of a minimal promoter and show it drives high luciferase activity in the same cell type

rubric: Necessity needs loss of function at the native locus.
Reporter assays show sufficiency; ChIP and overexpression show only association.

multivariable-calculus--nov-c1-sc1.prompt: What does the partial derivative of f(x, y) with respect to x measure?

options.label: The rate of change of f as x varies, y held fixed
The total accumulated area under f as x increases along the x-axis
The rate of change of f as both x and y vary together at a point
The slope of f along the direction of steepest ascent at a point

rubric: Partial derivative holds the other variables constant.
Distractors confuse it with total change or the gradient direction.

multivariable-calculus--prf-c5-sc2.prompt: You need the exact work done by F = (2xy + z, x^2, x) along a long, twisting path from A to B. Criteria: an exact answer with the least computation. Which approach is best?

options.label: Apply Green's theorem to the path, converting the line integral into a double integral of the curl
Close the path with a straight segment and apply Stokes' theorem, which avoids the twisting portion
Verify curl F = 0, find the potential f = x^2 y + xz, and compute f(B) - f(A)
Parametrize the path and integrate F·r'(t) numerically, since a path-specific integral cannot be avoided

rubric: curl F = 0 on R^3, so F is conservative and the work equals the potential difference regardless of path.
Distractors keep path dependence or misapply Green's and Stokes' theorems.

music-theory--adb-c2-sc3.prompt: In 4/4, where the quarter note gets one beat, how long does a dotted quarter note last?

options.label: One beat, since a dot only changes the look
One and a half beats
Three beats, since a dot triples the value
Two beats, since a dot doubles the value

rubric: A dot adds half the note's value, so a quarter plus an eighth equals one and a half beats.
Two beats confuses the dot with doubling the value.

music-theory--nov-c1-sc3.prompt: In 4/4 time, what does the top number tell you?

options.label: Number of measures in the piece
Which note gets the beat
Tempo in beats per minute
Beats per measure

rubric: The top number gives beats per measure.
The bottom number gives the note value that gets the beat.

music-theory--prf-c4-sc3.prompt: In C major, a phrase ends C/G (C major chord with G in the bass) – G7 – C. What is the best functional analysis of the C/G chord?

options.label: A subdominant-function chord, because the G in the bass is the root of V and the C and E above it behave like a IV chord
A tonic-function chord that arrives early, because C/G is a tonic triad and the G7 that follows is only a passing chord
A tonic in second inversion that closes the phrase, so the G7 and C that follow work as an added extension
A cadential six-four: it decorates the dominant, and its C and E fall to B and D

rubric: The cadential six-four sounds over the dominant bass and resolves C to B and E to D, so it functions as V, not I.
Distractors read it by its chord name or inversion alone and ignore its dominant function.

negotiation--cmp-c3-sc5.prompt: A vendor says: 'We can only do 10 percent off, and that is our final offer.' You still need a lower total cost. Which response applies the standard technique of expanding the options?

options.label: Restate your original price firmly and wait for the vendor to respond, since persistence usually wears down a stated limit
Ask the vendor's manager to override the discount without explaining why, since a higher authority can waive any limit
Say you will walk away unless they match your original number, so they see your alternative is credible and concede
Accept the 10 percent but ask for free delivery, longer payment terms or a warranty

rubric: Trading on other terms adds value without forcing the vendor to cut price further.
The other options repeat positions or escalate rather than create new options.

negotiation--cmp-c4-sc3.prompt: In a negotiation you offered 20 percent more volume for a lower unit price, and the supplier refused even though that is profitable for them. Which is the most plausible cause to investigate?

options.label: Capacity is limited, so extra volume is a risk, not a gain
The supplier is anchored on its list price and sees any discount as a precedent for other buyers
The supplier values volume less than you assumed, so a bigger discount would have worked
The supplier is bluffing to test your resolve, and a repeat of the same offer will be accepted

rubric: An offer's value depends on the other party's constraints, so test hidden constraints such as capacity.
The other explanations are unsupported or ignore the specific facts.

negotiation--cmp-c4-sc5.prompt: You compare two deals: Deal X pays 120,000 now, while Deal Y pays 100,000 now and 30,000 in a year with a 40 percent chance the buyer defaults. What does the comparison show about expected value if default means no payment?

options.label: X and Y are equal, since the 30,000 is offset by the 40 percent risk
Y is worth 112,000 in expectation, so X is better only if you ignore risk
Y is worth 118,000 in expectation, so X is higher
Y is worth 130,000 in expectation, so Y is clearly better than X

rubric: Expected value of Y is 100,000 + 0.6 x 30,000 = 118,000, below X.
Ignoring the default probability or miscalculating leads to the wrong comparison.

negotiation--nov-c2-sc2.prompt: Two sisters both want the same orange. One needs the peel for baking and the other wants the juice. What does this show?

options.label: Opposed positions may hide compatible interests
Hiding your needs from the other side usually gets you the best result
Splitting the item down the middle is usually the fairest way to settle
The sister with the stronger claim should get the whole orange

rubric: Different interests behind the same position allow both to gain.
Splitting misses the value-creating solution.

negotiation--nov-c2-sc4.prompt: A job candidate's lowest acceptable salary is 60,000 and the employer's highest is 55,000. What is the likely outcome?

options.label: They will probably settle near the midpoint of 57,500, since both sides usually split the gap
The candidate's walk-away point must be wrong, since a real offer would have to fall inside it
The employer's maximum will rise to match, since firms always stretch a budget to hire
No zone of agreement exists, so salary alone cannot close a deal

rubric: No overlap means no ZOPA on salary alone.
Midpoint deals need an overlap; other issues might change it.

negotiation--prf-c4-sc5.prompt: In three rounds you moved your price by 10, 5 and 2 points while the other side moved nothing. Which diagnosis fits best?

options.label: Their zero movement shows your price still sits above their reservation point, so keep conceding in shrinking steps until they respond and the gap closes
Shrinking steps signalled you were near your limit, so they will now accept; the right move is to hold the last number and wait for their answer
The opening 10-point move was too large; starting at 5 would have triggered reciprocity and produced matching moves from them in every later round
Unreciprocated concessions signalled spare room and taught them waiting pays; tie each move to a matching move

rubric: Giving without reciprocation teaches the other side that holding out is rewarded.
Distractors misread their silence as acceptance or blame the size of the first step.

neuroscience--cmp-c3-sn1.prompt: In a patch-clamp experiment on a neuron, chloride's equilibrium potential is -70 mV. The cell is held at -40 mV, and a GABA-A receptor agonist is applied so that the channels open. What happens to chloride?

options.label: Cl- flows out of the cell, because the interior is more positive than outside
No net Cl- flow, because the channels pass current only at the resting potential
Cl- flows into the cell, driving Vm toward -70 mV
Cl- flows into the cell, because it is negatively charged, driving Vm toward 0 mV

rubric: At -40 mV the membrane is above E_Cl, so the driving force pushes Cl- inward and moves Vm toward -70 mV.
Distractors reverse the direction of the driving force or ignore the equilibrium potential.

nextjs--cmp-c3-sc5.prompt: All pages under `/dashboard` must share a sidebar that stays mounted while navigating between them. Where do you put it?

options.label: In each `page.tsx`, importing a shared Sidebar component so every dashboard page renders it
In `app/dashboard/layout.tsx`, rendering `{children}` beside it
In `app/layout.tsx`, shown only when `usePathname()` starts with `/dashboard`, so it also wraps unrelated routes
In `app/dashboard/template.tsx`, which wraps children and keeps its state between navigations

rubric: Nested layouts persist across navigation between child routes and wrap their children.
Importing into each page remounts it, and the root layout is the wrong scope.

nextjs--cmp-c4-sc4.prompt: A Server Action inserts a row, and the DB confirms it, but the list page still shows old data until a hard rebuild. The page fetches the list in a Server Component. What is the likely missing piece?

options.label: The list should be fetched in `useEffect` on the client, because Server Components cannot show data that changed after build time
The action should return the new row to the browser, because the page re-renders only from values the action returns
The action needs to be declared inside a Client Component, because only client code can trigger a re-render of the list page
The action never invalidates cached data, such as with `revalidatePath('/list')`

rubric: Cached server-rendered output stays stale until invalidated with revalidatePath or revalidateTag.
Moving the fetch or the action location does not invalidate the cache.

nextjs--exp-c5-sn1.prompt: A site reads `cookies()` in the root layout to show a greeting. The team notices that all marketing pages are now rendered per request and CDN hit rates dropped. Judged by keeping marketing pages static while retaining the greeting, which fix is best?

options.label: Keep the cookie read in the root layout and add `revalidate = 3600` to each marketing page so the CDN caches them for an hour
Replace `cookies()` with `localStorage` read in the root layout Server Component, so no request-time API is used on the server
Move the greeting into a small component inside `<Suspense>` so only that part is dynamic
Set `dynamic = 'force-static'` on the root layout and keep reading `cookies()` there so every page below it is built statically

rubric: Request-time APIs make everything above them dynamic; isolating them keeps other routes static.
A revalidate time does not override dynamic APIs, localStorage is unavailable on the server, and forcing static would break the cookie read.

nextjs--exp-c6-sc4.prompt: Design a comment form. Constraints: it must submit and show validation errors even if JavaScript has not loaded, and it should show the new comment instantly when JavaScript is available. Which design meets both?

options.label: A Client Component form calling `fetch` in an `onSubmit` handler that always uses `preventDefault`, with errors held in `useState` and the new comment added to local state at once
A Server Action bound to the form's `action`, with `useActionState` for errors and `useOptimistic` for the instant item
A Route Handler called from `useEffect` after the user finishes typing, with the response stored in state so the new comment and any errors render immediately
A Server Action called only from an `onClick` handler on a plain button outside any form, wrapped in `useTransition` so the pending comment renders instantly

rubric: Form actions work as native form posts without JS, and the hooks add enhancement when JS runs.
Handlers that depend on JS events fail before hydration.

nosql-databases--prf-c5-sc5.prompt: Redis is proposed as the sole store for order records. Config: RDB snapshot every 5 minutes, no replicas. Requirement: lose at most about one second of orders after a crash. Which change best meets it at modest cost?

options.label: Enable AOF with fsync every second, and add a replica for failover
Shorten the RDB snapshot interval to 60 seconds, which cuts the loss window sufficiently
Raise the instance's memory limit so snapshots are never evicted before the next one
Switch the eviction policy to `allkeys-lru` so older orders are dropped before new ones

rubric: AOF with everysec bounds loss to about one second, and a replica improves recovery.
A 60-second snapshot still risks a minute of loss; memory limits and eviction do not bound crash loss.

nutrition--cmp-c4-sc3.prompt: A strict vegan who takes no supplements reports fatigue, pale skin and tingling in the hands and feet. Which deficiency best explains this pattern, given the diet?

options.label: Vitamin C, since citrus fruit is the main source and vegans often eat little of it
Vitamin K, since leafy greens are the main source and vegans often eat few
Vitamin B12, which plant foods do not reliably supply
Vitamin A, since orange produce is the main source and vegans often eat little

rubric: B12 is found almost only in animal foods, and deficiency causes anaemia and nerve symptoms.
The other vitamins are plentiful in plant foods and do not cause this combination.

object-oriented-programming--prf-c5-sc1.prompt: A game has enemies that can fly, swim, shoot and explode, in many combinations that designers change often. Criteria: avoid class explosion, allow behaviour changes without editing existing classes, keep the design simple. Which approach is best?

options.label: A single `Enemy` class with boolean flags and large conditionals checking them in every method, so one class holds all the behaviour
A deep hierarchy with one subclass for every combination, such as `FlyingShootingEnemy`, so each enemy type is fully explicit
Multiple inheritance of every capability into one large class and disabling unused ones at runtime through configuration
An `Enemy` composed of swappable movement and attack strategy objects, configured per enemy

rubric: Composition with strategies handles combinations without subclass explosion and permits runtime changes.
Hierarchies explode and flags centralise conditionals, which breaks open-closed.

observability-monitoring--prf-c5-sc2.prompt: Criteria: retain every trace containing an error or a request over 2s, and keep tracing cost under budget at 50k requests per second. Which sampling design is best?

options.label: Head-based sampling at 100% with seven-day retention, because full capture guarantees no error or slow trace is lost
Head-based sampling at 1% in each service, because the random choice keeps a fair share of error and slow traces
Tail-based sampling in a collector that keeps errors, slow traces and a few others
Head-based sampling that raises the rate to 20% for services with recent alerts, because it targets problem services

rubric: Only tail-based sampling can decide after seeing errors and duration.
Head sampling drops most error traces; full capture breaks the cost limit.

operating-systems--adb-c2-sc3.prompt: What is the main job of a process's page table?

options.label: It records the CPU registers saved when a process is paused
It lists which processes are ready to run and in what order
It stores the directories and files kept on a disk partition
It maps virtual pages to physical frames in RAM

rubric: The page table translates virtual page numbers to physical frame numbers.
Distractors describe the ready queue, the file system, and the saved context.

operating-systems--nov-c2-sc3.prompt: Why can a computer with 8 GB of RAM run programs whose combined memory needs exceed 8 GB?

options.label: The OS compresses every program to about half its size when loading it
Pages not currently in use can be moved to disk
The CPU keeps the overflow data in its registers and caches
Programs are made to share one copy of memory without isolation

rubric: Virtual memory swaps or pages unused data to disk.
Registers are far too small to hold the overflow.

organic-chemistry--prf-c5-sc2.prompt: Criteria: convert 1-bromobutane into butan-1-amine (same carbon count) with minimal over-alkylation to secondary and tertiary amines, using reliable, well-precedented steps. Which route is best?

options.label: Treat with NaCN, then reduce with LiAlH4, since nitrile reduction gives a primary amine selectively and avoids any alkylation of the product
Treat with one equivalent of NH3 in ethanol, since limiting the nucleophile prevents further alkylation of the product amine
Treat with NaNH2 in liquid ammonia, since the amide anion is a stronger nucleophile than ammonia and reacts faster than the product
Treat with potassium phthalimide, then hydrazine, since the imide N can be alkylated only once

rubric: Gabriel synthesis alkylates a nitrogen that cannot be alkylated twice, then releases the primary amine without chain change.
Direct ammonia alkylation over-alkylates, the nitrile route adds a carbon, and NaNH2 mainly causes elimination.

pandas--prf-c5-sc3.prompt: A 20 GB CSV must be summed by `category` on a 16 GB machine. Criteria: stay within memory, read the file once, give exact totals. Which approach is best?

options.label: Load the file with `read_csv(low_memory=False)` and drop the unused columns after loading, then run a single groupby sum
Read a random 10% sample with `skiprows`, sum each category, and scale the sums up by ten to estimate totals
Load the whole file once with `dtype=object` so no values are converted wrongly, then run a single groupby sum
Use `read_csv(chunksize=...)` with `usecols`, and add up each chunk's groupby sums

rubric: Chunked reading with incremental aggregation keeps memory bounded and totals exact.
Loading everything or sampling breaks the memory or exactness criterion.

people-management--nov-c1-sn1.prompt: Priya, one of your reports, has missed three deadlines this month. You are a new manager and want to address it. According to standard practice, what should you do first?

options.label: Wait until the annual review so you can raise the whole pattern with her
Mention it in the team meeting as a general reminder to everyone on time
Ask her peers whether they have noticed the same delays in her work
Meet her privately and give specific examples

rubric: Address issues early, privately and with specific examples.
Public hints, waiting, or polling peers delay or undermine a direct conversation.

personal-finance--adb-c2-sc3.prompt: Which of these is a fixed expense in a monthly budget?

options.label: Dining out at restaurants and cafes
Electricity bill that changes with usage
Rent set by a lease
Weekly grocery spending on food

rubric: A fixed expense stays the same each month, like rent under a lease.
Groceries, utilities and dining vary with use or choice.

personal-finance--prf-c5-sc1.prompt: Priya, 28, is in the 12% bracket and expects to be in the 24% bracket in retirement. She does not need a deduction now and wants to minimize lifetime tax on retirement savings. Which contribution type best meets her criteria?

options.label: Traditional contributions, since a deduction now is worth more than tax-free withdrawals later
Taxable brokerage investing, because it avoids all retirement account rules and tax drag
Roth contributions, paying 12% now to avoid 24% tax on withdrawals
Traditional contributions, because the tax rate on withdrawals will match her current rate

rubric: Paying tax at a lower rate now and avoiding a higher rate later minimizes lifetime tax.
Distractors ignore the expected rate difference or assume the rates will match.

personal-finance--prf-c5-sc2.prompt: A household has a full emergency fund and captures its employer match. Its goal is to be debt-free in 8 years with the least chance of missing that date, and its risk tolerance is low. Extra cash can prepay a 5.5% fixed mortgage or buy stock index funds. Which is best?

options.label: Invest in index funds, because stocks have historically beaten 5.5% over most 8-year periods and the gains could pay off the loan sooner
Hold the cash in savings, because prepayment is irreversible and a liquid balance can still cover the payoff at the end
Invest in index funds, because the higher expected return outweighs short-term volatility when the horizon is 8 years
Prepay the mortgage, since a certain 5.5% return suits a low risk tolerance

rubric: A guaranteed return that meets the deadline fits the stated criteria of low risk and a fixed target date.
Distractors assert stock outperformance as certain or ignore the risk criterion.

photography--prf-c5-sc5.prompt: A photographer wants to portray a busy market's energy. Criteria: show movement, keep one stall owner recognisable. Which technique best satisfies both?

options.label: Wide aperture f/1.4 at 1/500s, so the crowd blurs from shallow depth of field while the owner stays sharp
Panning at 1/30s to follow a passerby, so the moving shopper is sharp against a streaked background
Handheld 1/2000s, which freezes the crowd and the owner equally and shows no sense of motion
Tripod at 1/8s, owner standing still while crowd blurs

rubric: A slow shutter on a tripod blurs moving people while a still subject stays sharp.
Freezing everything loses movement, and the other options lose the owner.

options.label: The JSON object {"a": 1}
NULL because the key is quoted
A syntax error from the cast
The text value 1

rubric: `->>` extracts a field as text, giving 1.
`->` would return JSON; the other options misread the operator or cast.

postgresql--nov-c2-sn1.prompt: A table `users` has 10 million rows. The query `SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = 'a@example.com'` is slow, and `EXPLAIN` shows a `Seq Scan`. The `email` column has no index. Why is the query slow?

options.label: SELECT * makes Postgres take a lock on the whole table while it reads
Seq Scans are slow on large tables because they read rows from disk in random order
Postgres cannot compare a text column to a literal without casting every value first
With no index on email, Postgres must read every row

rubric: Without an index the planner must check every row, which is costly at 10 million rows.
Distractors blame text filtering, locking or scans in general rather than the missing index.

probability--cmp-c3-sc4.prompt: 2% of a population has a condition. A test is positive for 90% of people who have it and for 10% of people who do not. A person tests positive. What is the probability they have the condition?

options.label: 2%, the base rate
90%, the sensitivity
1.8%, the true positives
About 15.5%

rubric: 90% confuses P(positive | condition) with P(condition | positive), ignoring the low base rate.

probability--cmp-c4-sc5.prompt: Var(X) = 4 and Y = 2X. A colleague computes Var(X+Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y) = 20. What is Var(X+Y)?

options.label: 36, since X+Y = 3X, so Var(X+Y) = 9 × 4
20, since Var(X) + Var(Y) = 4 + 16, and variances always add for sums
12, since X+Y = 3X and variance scales linearly: Var(3X) = 3 × 4
16, since Y = 2X is the larger term, so Var(Y) = 16 sets the total

rubric: Variances add only for independent variables; here X+Y = 3X, so Var = 9·4 = 36.
12 forgets that variance scales with the square of the constant.

probability--nov-c1-sc5.prompt: What is the expected value of a random variable?

options.label: The gap between its largest and smallest possible values
Its middle value when the outcomes are sorted in order
Its probability-weighted average value
The single outcome with the highest probability of occurring

rubric: Expected value is the sum of each value times its probability.
Mode and median are different summaries of a distribution.

product-management--nov-c2-sn1.prompt: A sales rep asks the product manager to build a custom feature because one large prospect requested it. The PM has not heard this need from other customers. What is the best way to understand and respond to this request?

options.label: Check whether the underlying problem affects many users
Add it to the roadmap with a firm date to keep sales and the prospect happy
Build it first, since requests from the largest customers outrank other work
Reject it, since requests passed on by sales are never valid product input

rubric: A single request is a signal to investigate, not an automatic commitment.
Distractors either obey or dismiss the request without evidence.

programming-fundamentals--nov-c2-sc2.prompt: In Python, what does `"3" + "4"` produce, and why?

options.label: `7`, because plus always adds numbers together
An error, because text cannot be added at all
`"7"`, because digits are summed automatically
`"34"`, because plus joins strings

rubric: Quoted values are strings, and + on strings concatenates them.
Distractors assume digits in quotes are still numbers.

project-management--nov-c2-sc3.prompt: A task on the critical path slips by 3 days and nothing else changes. What happens to the project end date?

options.label: It moves later by fewer than 3 days in every case
It moves later only if the budget also increases
It moves later by 3 days
It stays the same, because other tasks absorb the delay

rubric: Critical path tasks have no float, so any slip delays the finish by the same amount.
Distractors assume float or budget changes that the critical path does not have.

psychology-fundamentals--cmp-c3-sc1.prompt: After a bout of food poisoning from shrimp salad, Dana now feels nauseated whenever she sees shrimp. In classical conditioning terms, what is the conditioned stimulus?

options.label: The shrimp salad she ate while sick
The illness caused by the bacteria
The sight of shrimp
The nausea she feels when she sees shrimp

rubric: The sight of shrimp was neutral, was paired with illness, and now triggers nausea, so it is the CS.
Distractors confuse the CS with the conditioned response (nausea at the sight) or the unconditioned stimulus (illness).

psychology-fundamentals--nov-c2-sc2.prompt: A child gets a sticker each time she puts her toys away, and she begins tidying more often. What does this illustrate?

options.label: Positive reinforcement
Punishment decreasing a behavior
Negative reinforcement removing a stimulus
Extinction of a learned response

rubric: Adding a pleasant stimulus that increases behavior is positive reinforcement.
Negative reinforcement removes an unpleasant stimulus; here nothing is removed.

quantum-mechanics--nov-c2-sc1.prompt: Why must the wavefunction of a particle in an infinite square well be zero at the walls?

options.label: The wavefunction must be zero everywhere inside the well as well, since energy is quantized there
ψ is zero outside the infinite potential and must be continuous
The particle loses all of its kinetic energy whenever it touches a wall, so ψ drops to zero there
The walls reflect the particle perfectly, so it is never found at the walls themselves

rubric: Zero probability outside plus continuity forces ψ=0 at the walls.
Other options give classical pictures that do not explain the boundary condition.

react--cmp-c4-sc4.prompt: A component builds `const options = { page, sort };` in its body, then runs `useEffect(() => { fetchData(options).then(setRows); }, [options]);`. The network is hit continuously. What is the root cause?

options.label: `options` is a new object every render, so the effect re-runs each time
`setRows` is missing from the dependency array, so React re-runs the effect after every state update
Objects cannot be listed as dependencies, so React re-runs the effect on every single render
`fetchData` returns a promise, and effects may not start asynchronous work without cleanup

rubric: Dependencies compare by reference; a fresh object each render triggers the effect, which sets state and renders again.
